title: Zeroth Cech set of a covering and the plus construction of a presheaf of sets on a site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\mathcal F$ a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, i.e. a functor $\mathcal C^{op}\to$ sets; for $h:V\to W$ write $s\mapsto s|_V=\mathcal F(h)(s)$. (a) *Zeroth Cech set.* For a covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ put $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\{(s_i)_{i\in I}\in\prod_i\mathcal F(U_i)\mid s_i|_{U_i\times_UU_j}=s_j|_{U_i\times_UU_j}\ \forall i,j\in I\}$ (restrictions along the two projections of the fibre product), with the canonical map $\mathcal F(U)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $s\mapsto(s|_{U_i})_i$. (b) *Morphisms of coverings.* A morphism (refinement) $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ from $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ to $\mathcal V=\{V_j\to V\}_{j\in J}$ consists of a morphism $\chi:U\to V$, a map $\alpha:I\to J$ and morphisms $f_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ such that $U_i\xrightarrow{f_i}V_{\alpha(i)}\to V$ equals $U_i\to U\xrightarrow{\chi}V$ for all $i$; it is said to lie over $\chi$. It induces $f^*:H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $(f^*s)_i=s_{\alpha(i)}|_{U_i}$ (restriction along $f_i$), which is well defined because $f_i\times f_{i'}$ maps $U_i\times_UU_{i'}$ to $V_{\alpha(i)}\times_VV_{\alpha(i')}$ compatibly with the projections, and $f^*$ is compatible with $\mathcal F(\chi):\mathcal F(V)\to\mathcal F(U)$ and the canonical maps of (a). A covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$ *refines* a covering $\mathcal V$ of $U$ if there is a morphism $\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$. (c) *The plus construction.* Let $\mathcal J_U$ be the category whose objects are the coverings of $U$ and whose morphisms are the morphisms of coverings over $\mathrm{id}_U$ (it is small by the set-theoretic conventions of a site and nonempty, containing $\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$); $\mathcal U\mapsto H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $f\mapsto f^*$ is a functor $\mathcal J_U^{opp}\to$ sets. Define $\mathcal F^+(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal J_U^{opp}}H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ (colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) and write $[\mathcal U,s]\in\mathcal F^+(U)$ for the image of $s\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$. For a morphism $h:V\to U$, choose for every covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$ the fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ (axiom (iii) of a site); the covering $\mathcal U\times_UV=\{U_i\times_UV\to V\}$ and the projections give a morphism of coverings $p_{\mathcal U}:\mathcal U\times_UV\to\mathcal U$ over $h$, natural in $\mathcal U\in\mathcal J_U$, and $\mathcal F^+(h):\mathcal F^+(U)\to\mathcal F^+(V)$ is the induced map of colimits, $[\mathcal U,s]\mapsto[\mathcal U\times_UV,p_{\mathcal U}^*s]$, i.e. $(s_i)\mapsto(s_i|_{U_i\times_UV})$. Finally $\theta_U:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F^+(U)$, $s\mapsto[\{\mathrm{id}_U\},s]$, using $H^0(\{\mathrm{id}_U\},\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(U)$. That these data form a presheaf $\mathcal F^+$ (independent of the choices of fibre products) with a morphism of presheaves $\theta:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^+$ is a lemma (Stacks Sites, Lemma 00W4), stated as a node of its own.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1 (section-sheafification): the definition of $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ and of the maps induced by morphisms of coverings, the category $\mathcal J_U$ and $\mathcal F^+(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal J_U^{opp}}H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, the restriction maps via $\mathcal J_U\to\mathcal J_V$, and the map $\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F^+(U)$ from the trivial covering; morphisms of coverings as in Sites, Definition 00VT (definition-morphism-coverings)

proof.text: *(a) $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ and the canonical map are well defined.* For a covering $\mathcal U=\{\pi_i:U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and $i,j\in I$, axiom (iii) of a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] applied to $\mathcal U$ and $\pi_j:U_j\to U$ gives that the fibre product $U_i\times_UU_j$ exists; choose one, with projections $\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2$. The condition $\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_1)(s_i)=\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_2)(s_j)$ does not depend on the choice: another choice $P'$ is related to $P$ by the unique isomorphism $\phi:P'\to P$ with $\mathrm{pr}_k\phi=\mathrm{pr}'_k$, and $\mathcal F(\phi)$ is a bijection with $\mathcal F(\phi)\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_k)=\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}'_k)$. So $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is a well-defined subset of the set $\prod_i\mathcal F(U_i)$ ($I$ is a set and each $\mathcal F(U_i)$ is a set). For $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, the family $(\mathcal F(\pi_i)s)_i$ lies in it: $\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_1)\mathcal F(\pi_i)s=\mathcal F(\pi_i\mathrm{pr}_1)s=\mathcal F(\pi_j\mathrm{pr}_2)s=\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_2)\mathcal F(\pi_j)s$, since $\pi_i\mathrm{pr}_1=\pi_j\mathrm{pr}_2$ (fibre product square) and $\mathcal F$ is a functor on $\mathcal C^{op}$.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1 (section-sheafification), the paragraphs before Lemma 00W4 (lemma-plus-presheaf): definition of $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ and the canonical map $\mathcal F(U)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$

proof.text: *(b) Morphisms of coverings compose, and $f^*$ is well defined.* Let $f=(\chi,\alpha,(f_i))$ be a morphism from $\mathcal U=\{\pi_i:U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ to $\mathcal V=\{\rho_j:V_j\to V\}_{j\in J}$, so $\rho_{\alpha(i)}f_i=\chi\pi_i$. Composition with $g=(\psi,\beta,(g_j)):\mathcal V\to\mathcal W=\{\sigma_k:W_k\to W\}$ is $g\circ f=(\psi\chi,\beta\alpha,(g_{\alpha(i)}f_i)_i)$, again a morphism since $\sigma_{\beta\alpha(i)}g_{\alpha(i)}f_i=\psi\rho_{\alpha(i)}f_i=\psi\chi\pi_i$; the identity of $\mathcal U$ is $(\mathrm{id}_U,\mathrm{id}_I,(\mathrm{id}_{U_i}))$; associativity and the unit laws hold componentwise (composition in $\mathcal C$ and of maps of sets). For $i,i'\in I$ the morphisms $f_i\mathrm{pr}_1:U_i\times_UU_{i'}\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ and $f_{i'}\mathrm{pr}_2:U_i\times_UU_{i'}\to V_{\alpha(i')}$ satisfy $\rho_{\alpha(i)}f_i\mathrm{pr}_1=\chi\pi_i\mathrm{pr}_1=\chi\pi_{i'}\mathrm{pr}_2=\rho_{\alpha(i')}f_{i'}\mathrm{pr}_2$, so by the universal property of $V_{\alpha(i)}\times_VV_{\alpha(i')}$ (which exists by Step 1) there is $f_i\times f_{i'}$ with $\mathrm{pr}_1(f_i\times f_{i'})=f_i\mathrm{pr}_1$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2(f_i\times f_{i'})=f_{i'}\mathrm{pr}_2$. For $s=(s_j)\in H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)$ put $(f^*s)_i=\mathcal F(f_i)(s_{\alpha(i)})$. Then $\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_1)(f^*s)_i=\mathcal F(f_i\times f_{i'})\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_1)(s_{\alpha(i)})=\mathcal F(f_i\times f_{i'})\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_2)(s_{\alpha(i')})=\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_2)(f^*s)_{i'}$, the middle equality being the condition on $s$ for the pair $(\alpha(i),\alpha(i'))$. So $f^*s\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ and $f^*:H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is a map of sets.

source.place: Sites, Definition 00VT (definition-morphism-coverings) for morphisms of families; Sites, Section 00W1 (section-sheafification), the paragraphs before Lemma 00W4 (lemma-plus-presheaf): the diagram with $U_i\times_UU_j\to V_{\alpha(i)}\times_VV_{\alpha(j)}$ and the induced map $H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$

proof.text: *(b) $f^*$ is functorial and compatible with $\mathcal F(\chi)$.* With the notation of Step 2: $((g\circ f)^*s)_i=\mathcal F(g_{\alpha(i)}f_i)(s_{\beta\alpha(i)})=\mathcal F(f_i)\mathcal F(g_{\alpha(i)})(s_{\beta(\alpha(i))})=(f^*(g^*s))_i$, so $(g\circ f)^*=f^*\circ g^*$; and $(\mathrm{id}^*s)_i=\mathcal F(\mathrm{id}_{U_i})s_i=s_i$, so $\mathrm{id}^*=\mathrm{id}$. For $t\in\mathcal F(V)$, $(f^*(\mathcal F(\rho_j)t)_j)_i=\mathcal F(f_i)\mathcal F(\rho_{\alpha(i)})t=\mathcal F(\rho_{\alpha(i)}f_i)t=\mathcal F(\chi\pi_i)t=\mathcal F(\pi_i)(\mathcal F(\chi)t)$, i.e. $f^*$ composed with the canonical map of $\mathcal V$ equals the canonical map of $\mathcal U$ composed with $\mathcal F(\chi)$.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1 (section-sheafification), the paragraphs before Lemma 00W4 (lemma-plus-presheaf): the map $H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is compatible with $\mathcal F(V)\to\mathcal F(U)$; contravariance in the paragraph defining $\mathcal J_U$

proof.text: *(c) $\mathcal J_U$ is a small nonempty category, $H^0(-,\mathcal F)$ a functor on $\mathcal J_U^{opp}$, and $\mathcal F^+(U)$ exists.* The objects of $\mathcal J_U$ are the coverings of $U$, a subset of the set $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; the morphisms $\mathcal U'\to\mathcal U$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ are pairs $(\alpha,(f_{i'}))$, elements of the set $\operatorname{Map}(I',I)\times\prod_{i'\in I'}\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal C)$ ($\operatorname{Ob}$ and $\operatorname{Mor}$ of a site are sets). Composition and identities of Step 2 preserve the condition $\chi=\mathrm{id}_U$ ($\mathrm{id}_U\mathrm{id}_U=\mathrm{id}_U$), so $\mathcal J_U$ is a small category; it contains $\{\mathrm{id}_U:U\to U\}$ by axiom (i). By Step 3, $\mathcal U\mapsto H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $f\mapsto f^*$ is a functor $D_U:\mathcal J_U^{opp}\to$ sets. A colimit of $D_U$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] exists: let $L$ be the quotient of the set $\coprod_{\mathcal U\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal J_U}H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ by the equivalence relation generated by $(\mathcal U',f^*s)\sim(\mathcal U,s)$ for $f:\mathcal U'\to\mathcal U$ in $\mathcal J_U$, and $\iota_{\mathcal U}(s)=[\mathcal U,s]$ the class; then $\iota_{\mathcal U'}\circ f^*=\iota_{\mathcal U}$ (cocone), and for a cocone $(M,(\mu_{\mathcal U}))$ the map $[\mathcal U,s]\mapsto\mu_{\mathcal U}(s)$ is well defined (it is constant on generating pairs since $\mu_{\mathcal U'}f^*=\mu_{\mathcal U}$, hence on classes), is the unique map $u$ with $u\iota_{\mathcal U}=\mu_{\mathcal U}$ (the $\iota_{\mathcal U}$ are jointly surjective). Hence $\mathcal F^+(U)$, the chosen colimit, and the classes $[\mathcal U,s]=\iota_{\mathcal U}(s)$ are defined.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1 (section-sheafification), the paragraphs before Lemma 00W4 (lemma-plus-presheaf): the paragraph defining $\mathcal J_U$ ('By our conventions on sites this is indeed a category ... $\Ob(\mathcal J_U)$ is not empty since $\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$ is an object') and $\mathcal F^+(U)=\colim_{\mathcal J_U^{opp}}H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$

proof.text: *(c) $\mathcal F^+(h)$ is well defined.* Let $h:V\to U$. For $\mathcal U=\{\pi_i:U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ in $\mathcal J_U$, axiom (iii) [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] gives the chosen fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ (projections $\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2$) and that $\mathcal U\times_UV=\{\mathrm{pr}_2:U_i\times_UV\to V\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering of $V$. Then $p_{\mathcal U}=(h,\mathrm{id}_I,(\mathrm{pr}_1)_i):\mathcal U\times_UV\to\mathcal U$ is a morphism of coverings over $h$, the condition $\pi_i\mathrm{pr}_1=h\,\mathrm{pr}_2$ being the fibre product square. For $g=(\alpha,(g_{i'})):\mathcal U'\to\mathcal U$ in $\mathcal J_U$ let $g_{i'}\times_UV:U'_{i'}\times_UV\to U_{\alpha(i')}\times_UV$ be the unique morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_1(g_{i'}\times_UV)=g_{i'}\mathrm{pr}_1$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2(g_{i'}\times_UV)=\mathrm{pr}_2$ (it exists since $\pi_{\alpha(i')}g_{i'}\mathrm{pr}_1=\pi'_{i'}\mathrm{pr}_1=h\,\mathrm{pr}_2$); $g_V=(\alpha,(g_{i'}\times_UV))$ is a morphism $\mathcal U'\times_UV\to\mathcal U\times_UV$ over $\mathrm{id}_V$, i.e. in $\mathcal J_V$, and by the uniqueness in the universal property $\mathcal U\mapsto\mathcal U\times_UV$, $g\mapsto g_V$ is a functor $\mathcal J_U\to\mathcal J_V$. Moreover $p_{\mathcal U}\circ g_V=g\circ p_{\mathcal U'}$ (both are $(h,\alpha,(g_{i'}\mathrm{pr}_1)_{i'})$, Step 2), so by Step 3 $g_V^*p_{\mathcal U}^*=p_{\mathcal U'}^*g^*$. Put $\varphi_{\mathcal U}=\iota^V_{\mathcal U\times_UV}\circ p_{\mathcal U}^*:H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to\mathcal F^+(V)$, with $\iota^V$ the coprojections of Step 4 for $V$. Then $\varphi_{\mathcal U'}g^*=\iota^V_{\mathcal U'\times_UV}g_V^*p_{\mathcal U}^*=\iota^V_{\mathcal U\times_UV}p_{\mathcal U}^*=\varphi_{\mathcal U}$, using the cocone property of $\iota^V$ for the morphism $g_V$ of $\mathcal J_V$. So $(\mathcal F^+(V),(\varphi_{\mathcal U}))$ is a cocone on $D_U$, and the universal property of the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives the unique $\mathcal F^+(h):\mathcal F^+(U)\to\mathcal F^+(V)$ with $\mathcal F^+(h)[\mathcal U,s]=[\mathcal U\times_UV,p_{\mathcal U}^*s]$, where $(p_{\mathcal U}^*s)_i=\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_1)(s_i)=s_i|_{U_i\times_UV}$ (Step 2). (That $\mathcal F^+$ is then a presheaf, independent of the choices, is not part of the definition.)

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1 (section-sheafification), the paragraphs before Lemma 00W4 (lemma-plus-presheaf): the paragraph with the functor $\mathcal J_U\to\mathcal J_V$, $\{U_i\to U\}\mapsto\{U_i\times_UV\to V\}$, the functorial morphism of coverings given by the projections, and the induced map $\mathcal F^+(U)\to\mathcal F^+(V)$ 'by generalities of colimits'

proof.text: *(c) $\theta_U$ is well defined.* $\{\mathrm{id}_U:U\to U\}$ is a covering by axiom (i) [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with a one-element index set. For the chosen fibre product $U\times_UU$ of $\mathrm{id}_U$ with itself the square gives $\mathrm{id}_U\mathrm{pr}_1=\mathrm{id}_U\mathrm{pr}_2$, so $\mathrm{pr}_1=\mathrm{pr}_2$ and the condition defining $H^0(\{\mathrm{id}_U\},\mathcal F)$ holds for every $s\in\mathcal F(U)$; thus $H^0(\{\mathrm{id}_U\},\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(U)$, and the canonical map of Step 1 is $s\mapsto\mathcal F(\mathrm{id}_U)s=s$. Hence $\theta_U=\iota_{\{\mathrm{id}_U\}}:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F^+(U)$, $s\mapsto[\{\mathrm{id}_U\},s]$, is a well-defined map of sets (Step 4). (That $\theta$ commutes with the maps $\mathcal F(h)$, $\mathcal F^+(h)$ is part of the lemma stated separately, not of this definition.)

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks Sites, Section 00W1 up to Lemma 00W4 (sites.tex 1631-1795) and Definition 00VT. The definition agrees with the source; statement unchanged except the bracket citation [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] for the colimit of sets (added to stmt_deps, since F^+(U) and the classes [U,s] are a chosen colimit). Six elementary well-definedness steps: (1) H^0 is a subset of prod F(U_i), independent of the chosen fibre products (axiom (iii)), and F(U)->H^0 lands in it; (2) morphisms of coverings compose (identities, associativity) and f^* lands in H^0 via f_i x f_i'; (3) (g o f)^* = f^* g^*, id^* = id, compatibility with F(chi); (4) J_U is a small nonempty category (Cov(C), Ob, Mor are sets by def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology; {id_U} by axiom (i)), H^0 a functor on J_U^opp, the colimit of sets constructed as a quotient of the disjoint union; (5) F^+(h): U x_U V is a covering (axiom (iii)), p_U a morphism over h, g -> g_V a functor J_U -> J_V with p_U g_V = g p_U', so the maps iota^V p_U^* form a cocone and induce F^+(h) with the stated formula; (6) H^0({id_U},F) = F(U) since pr1 = pr2 on U x_U U, theta_U = iota_{id_U}. No new nodes. The forward lemma lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf (presheaf, independence of choices, theta natural) is not cited. Mathlib re-searched (Loogle, LeanSearch, local_search, grep): Precoverage.ZeroHypercover with its Category instance is the covering-family J_U, PreZeroHypercover.pullback₁ the pulled-back covering, but there is no H^0 functor or colimit over it, so no leaf.
